title: Hansi Flick says he will retire from management when he leaves Barcelona
content:
Hansi Flick has revealed that the head coach role at Barcelona will be his final job in management.

Flick, 61, has been in charge of the Spanish side since the summer of 2024, and his contract is set to expire in the summer of 2027. Club president Joan Laporta said this week, however, that a contract-extension announcement for the head coach is imminent.

The German coach had recently been linked to other managerial roles in Europe, but speaking before his side’s Champions League round-of-16 second leg tie against Newcastle United, he dispelled those rumours by confirming that the Barcelona job will be the final role in a managerial career that began in 1996.

“Everyone knows I am really happy here. I need to speak with my family first, but we have enough time to discuss it,” Flick said on Tuesday.

“It’s clear that I love to work here. But the most important thing for me is that I have a fantastic family and I am proud of that. I feel the support of everyone in Barcelona.

“But, this is football, and we know how this world works. We (as a family) have no thoughts of leaving to (join) another club. This will be my last job, and I am really happy about that.”

Laporta spoke to radio station RAC1 about Flick after being re-elected until 2031 on Sunday.

“His contract runs up until 2027 now and we want him to work always with an extra year of contract ahead,” he said. “Hansi is also keen on that. We will try to announce it as soon as possible because we believe it’s the best for the club.

“Flick has added new elements to our team always respecting our style and philosophy, with discipline and self-demand. He has fixed the team and make it successful with the same players he inherited.”

Flick’s managerial career began in 1996 with German side FC Bammental.

He has had spells at Hoffenheim and RB Salzburg, in addition to working for the Germany national team and Bayern Munich, both as assistant manager and head coach. He has also been the sporting director for Hoffenheim and Germany.

Since replacing Xavi as Barcelona head coach in the summer of 2024, he has won four trophies with Barca, including the league title in his first campaign.

Barcelona will host Newcastle at Camp Nou on Wednesday, having drawn the first leg 1-1 at St James’ Park last Tuesday.
